correctness.rationale: For positive full-tree simplex summands, generic exposed vertices correspond bijectively to recursive subtree-maximizer choices. Independence of child-order permutations and their random interleaving proves the independent Bernoulli angle law; its squared sum gives the collision product. A minimal imbalanced node has perfect power-of-two child sizes and imbalance at least 1/3. Equality outside perfection requires a unique such node; if non-root, its parent would force a second imbalance. Thus the sharp normalized 10/9 gap and complete equality class are proved for all n. Exact checker reran all 64 plane-tree shapes of sizes 2 to 6 against rank permutations, 8-leaf tree gap checks, and dyadic families.

originality.rationale: The claim is a sharp all-dimensional geometric collision gap and rigidity/equality classification for the full-tree binary nestohedral realizations. Defant 2021/2023 establishes the fertilitope/binary-nestohedron equivalence; Postnikov–Reiner–Williams 2006/2007 establishes cubical combinatorics and cone-poset machinery. The general cone machinery can recover individual angles but the sharp gap and all-dimension equality classification are not statements in the inspected primary sections and are not formally implied by their enumerative conclusions alone. Alternative formulation risk is expressly retained.

value.rationale: A full-tree binary nestohedron is an intrinsic Euclidean realization of a fixed combinatorial cube but its Gaussian vertex distribution need not be uniform. The theorem classifies a natural continuum-independent geometric concentration invariant across all dimensions and exhibits a sharp forbidden interval and a rigidity/equality class in infinitely many dimensions. The six-leaf comparison gives a structural reason why balancing only the root fails to optimize directional vertex exposure. This is a motivated complete classification rather than a textbook restatement or a small numerical improvement.
